title: Review: jmap-mail-types crate (RFC 8621 wire types)
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — two P0 bugs (EmailComparator and EmailFilterCondition uncreatable from external crates) make the query module non-functional for its intended client use case. P1 risk: server serialization of empty-keyword emails violates RFC 8621.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the skip_serializing_if on default-value fields (P1) — could be intentional if jmap-mail-server always adds missing fields before sending; the PLAN.md does not clarify. Uncertainty driven by: not reading jmap-mail-server yet to see how it consumes Email serialization. Would raise confidence if: jmap-mail-server is read to confirm it does/does not rely on Email serialization for wire output.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — the macro-generated serde impls are clean, Borrow<str> on Keyword is idiomatic, no gratuitous clones, no unsafe. The #[non_exhaustive]-with-no-constructor pattern on input types is the main idiom failure.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: none. Uncertainty driven by: not having a compiler to confirm the non_exhaustive struct-update-syntax restriction applies in the exact Rust edition/version used (1.75).
